questions.prompt: The app runs in development mode with NgRx's default settings. What happens when `addPostSuccess` is dispatched?

code.label: posts.reducer.ts

options.text: An error: in development, NgRx freezes the state, so `push` throws
It works: the new post appears
Nothing visible: no error, but the screen doesn't update

questions.explanation: Reducers must return a new state object and never change the old one. NgRx's runtime checks freeze the state in development to catch this. Return `{ ...state, posts: [...state.posts, post] }`, or use the entity adapter: `adapter.addOne(post, state)`.

questions.prompt: After a successful login, this effect runs in an endless loop. Which version fixes it?

code.label: auth.effects.ts

questions.explanation: Whatever an effect emits is dispatched. After `tap` it still emits `loginSuccess`, so it triggers itself. `dispatch: false` tells NgRx this effect dispatches nothing. With `take(1)`, the effect finishes after the first login and never runs again. With `map`, it dispatches the `Promise` that `navigate` returns, and NgRx reports an invalid action.

questions.prompt: Opening the feed freezes the browser with endless requests. Click the buggy line.

code.label: posts.effects.ts

questions.explanation: On success the effect dispatches `loadFeed` again, which starts a new request, and so on forever. It should dispatch the success action with the data: `map((posts) => PostsActions.loadFeedSuccess({ posts }))`.

questions.prompt: `postsFeature` was created with `createFeature`, but its state was never registered with `provideState`. What happens when the feed reads `selectAll`?

code.label: app.config.ts

options.text: The console warns that the feature `posts` doesn't exist in the state, and the selectors fail
It works: `createFeature` registers the state by itself
The feed shows an empty list

questions.explanation: A feature's state only exists after `provideState(postsFeature)`, either here or in the route that lazy-loads the feed. Without it the feature selector returns `undefined`.

questions.prompt: Post `p1` is already in the store with 10 likes. After a like, the server returns `p1` with 11 likes. What goes in the gap so the post shows 11?
questions.explanation: `setOne` adds the post, or replaces it when the id already exists. `addOne` does nothing when the id exists, so the post would stay at 10 likes. `addMany` takes a list, and `removeOne` takes an id.

questions.prompt: The server sends three posts, but only one shows in the feed: the adapter looks for an `id` field. Which version fixes it?

context.label: posts.reducer.ts

options.code: export const adapter = createEntityAdapter<Post & { id: string }>();

questions.explanation: By default the adapter uses `entity.id`, which is `undefined` here, so all three posts get the same key. `selectId` tells it which field is the key. `sortComparer` only sorts. The third version doesn't build: `setAll` now expects posts with an `id`, and ours don't have one.

questions.prompt: A user likes a post. What should the post card do?

options.text: Emit an output; the container dispatches `PostsActions.likePost({ postId })`, and an effect calls the API
Call `postsApi.likePost()` and update the store when the response arrives
Update the post's like count with `store.select` and save it

questions.explanation: Presentational components only show data and emit events. The container turns the event into an action, the effect talks to the server, and the reducer updates the state. Every change shows up in Redux DevTools.

questions.prompt: Match each entity adapter method with what it does.

pairs.right: Adds the entity only if its id is new
Adds the entity, or replaces it if the id exists
Changes some fields of an entity that exists: `{ id, changes }`
Deletes the entity with this id

questions.explanation: Every method returns a new state and never changes the old one. Use `setAll` when the feed loads, `setOne` when the server sends back a whole post, and `updateOne` when you only know what changed.

questions.explanation: `selectSignal` returns a signal, which the template reads by calling it. `select` returns an observable, so `posts()` wouldn't build. `dispatch` sends actions, it doesn't read state.
